transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13
Start: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (Redwood CSM); Maya Rodriguez (Peregrine Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Sara Ng (Product PM), Devon Price (Security)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style checkin focused on launch readiness: capacity mapping for initial launch, cost guardrails, reliability SLOs, and security checklist (SOC2/KMS/VPC). Agreed to run a short performance snapshot using Peregrine traces and to align on dedicated vs hosted economics before pilot kickoff.

Topics:
- Current usage profile and traffic shape (burstiness, p95 latency targets)
- Cost tradeoffs: batching, quantization, caching, dedicated pools
- Reliability: SLOs, fallback policies, multi-region routing
- Security/compliance: SOC two, KMS integration, audit logs, VPC peering
- Next steps: perf snapshot, pricing model, pilot kickoff date

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, um, we'll run through the health readout and then jump into launch readiness items.
[00:12] Maya Rodriguez: hey Alex, thanks. excited to get this lined up, we've got GA planned for early December so timing's tight.
[00:20] Priya Mehta: cool, that's helpful context, Maya. can you just remind us, what percent of traffic is realtime chat vs async batch?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: um, right now it's about 70% realtime low-latency chat, 30% async batched reporting calls. peaks are around 3x baseline during promos — so bursty.
[00:44] Sara Ng: and p95 latency target is 300ms for chat, obviously lower is better but we need to be realistic.
[00:52] Alex Chen: perfect — so the two main levers we'll watch are batching for the 30% and caching/prefix reuse for chat to shave p95.
[01:04] Devon Price: quick security note — we'll need SOC2 in scope and we prefer customer-managed KMS for keys, is that supported?
[01:12] Priya Mehta: yes, Redwood supports customer KMS for Private deployments and there is an HSM option for on-prem. for hosted we have bring-your-key via KMS integration, slight lat penalty maybe, we'll quantify.
[01:25] Devon Price: okay good. also need audit logs and retention tbd, we'll send our policy.
[01:32] Jordan Blake: noted, we'll add audit log retention options to the security package we share.
[01:39] Alex Chen: quick baseline readout — over the last month your token burn averages ~1.4M tokens/day with spikes to 4.2M. cost modeling shows hosted at current settings is about $X/day, switching to dedicated reserved GPUs with 99th-percentile latency targets reduces unit cost ~30% for sustained usage, but committed monthly is required.
[02:05] Maya Rodriguez: can you unpack the latency vs cost tradeoff a bit — we can't sacrifice p95 too much.
[02:12] Priya Mehta: sure — two approaches. 1) hosted w/ autoscale: keeps latency low but cost rises on spikes. 2) dedicated with burst buffer: lower unit cost for steady state, plus burst capacity so p95 holds during promos. also caching saves tokens for repeated prefixes.
[02:31] Liam O'Connor: what's the operational overhead for dedicated? we prefer less hand-holding.
[02:36] Alex Chen: dedicated has a bit more config at setup — autoscale policies, model pinning, rollback policies — but Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards and auto-fallbacks to hosted if capacity saturates. SEs handle initial tuning.
[02:52] Sara Ng: are there SLOs/SLA numbers we can commit to?
[02:56] Jordan Blake: yes, for Dedicated we have SLA tiers with uptime and tail latency targets; we'll propose a baseline that meets your 300ms p95 for chat. SLA gets tighter with higher tiers.
[03:10] Maya Rodriguez: ok, we also have to meet internal security gating — anything special for VPC peering?
[03:17] Priya Mehta: VPC peering is supported for Private deployments — for hosted you can use VPC egress plus private endpoints. we do need some firewall rules and routing setup on your side, we'll share the network checklist.
[03:30] Liam O'Connor: good, send the checklist. also on the perf side, we want to see KV cache behavior because our prompts heavily reuse context.
[03:38] Priya Mehta: understood — we'll enable prefix/KV cache in the snapshot. small note: transcriptions sometimes say KV cash, ha, but it's KV cache — and our runtime preserves per-token cache to avoid recompute.
[03:52] Alex Chen: let's glue this into a plan. action: Priya will run a 24-hour perf snapshot using a sample of your traffic with cache and batching settings; that will show real p95 and cost per token with suggested quant configs.
[04:05] Maya Rodriguez: do you need synthetic traffic or real traces?
[04:10] Priya Mehta: sample traces are best — keeps fidelity. if you can't share raw traces, a sanitized sample works.
[04:16] Maya Rodriguez: we'll sanitize and share by Tuesday.
[04:20] Devon Price: on compliance, we need to see SOC2 cert and pen-test schedule.
[04:24] Jordan Blake: we can attach Redwood SOC2 report and our penetration test cadence in the security packet. we'll also include the audit-log export formats.
[04:34] Sara Ng: timeline question — you mentioned pilot kickoff?
[04:38] Alex Chen: yes, pilot kickoff targeted for 2025-11-24 — that's when we spin up the dedicated pool, run smoke tests, and validate failover.
[04:46] Maya Rodriguez: sounds tight but doable. what do you need from us before then?
[04:51] Alex Chen: three things: 1) traffic sample (sanitized) 2) confirmation of KMS preference and SOC2 scope 3) final list of top 10 high-traffic routes to pin for monitoring.
[05:03] Liam O'Connor: we'll get that.
[05:06] Priya Mehta: on model side, do you plan to use open-weights we host or bring-your-model for private infra?
[05:12] Maya Rodriguez: initial plan is to use a Redwood-verified open model for faster ops, but we may bring a tuned in-house model later.
[05:20] Priya Mehta: perfect — that path is straightforward. for bring-your-model on Private you'll need infra compatibility checks; we have a model-onboarding guide.
[05:31] Sara Ng: any quick wins on cost right now we can enable without changing infra?
[05:35] Priya Mehta: yes — enable KV cache and tweak request-level max_tokens and stop sequences plus a conservative quantization profile for non-chat routes; that typically saves 10-25% cost with minimal quality impact.
[05:48] Alex Chen: we also noticed a few long-running requests that look like exploratory queries — routing those to a cheaper model variant can save. we can set automated fallback rules.
[05:59] Maya Rodriguez: good point, we have internal experiments hitting prod. we'll gate those.
[06:04] Devon Price: clarifying encryption — do logs contain any PII by default?
[06:09] Jordan Blake: by default we redact known PII tokens in transit and at rest we encrypt with keys; retention is configurable per account. we'll show the log-redaction settings.
[06:21] Liam O'Connor: what's the telemetry for token-level cost? we want per-route breakdowns.
[06:26] Priya Mehta: Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-token cost breakdowns and you can attach tags to requests for downstream billing.
[06:33] Sara Ng: great. can we set alerts for token burn spikes?
[06:36] Alex Chen: yep, threshold alerts and anomaly detection can be configured.
[06:40] Maya Rodriguez: timeline check — after the perf snapshot, when do we expect a recommendation?
[06:45] Priya Mehta: snapshot done by 11/20, analysis two working days after, so target 11/22 for recommendations.
[06:52] Alex Chen: and pricing sheet by 11/17 as I mentioned.
[06:55] Devon Price: one more security ask — can we get a network flow diagram for hosted and Private?
[07:01] Jordan Blake: yes, we'll include network diagrams in the packet.
[07:05] Maya Rodriguez: thanks. shifting to runbook — who owns incident response on day zero?
[07:10] Alex Chen: during pilot Redwood will own first-level rollback and troubleshooting; we'll pair with your on-call and then hand over runbook ops post-stabilization.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: ok, define the escalation path and RTO targets.
[07:24] Jordan Blake: we'll include an escalation matrix and RTO/RPO in the runbook.
[07:31] Priya Mehta: quick technical aside — for your prompt reuse pattern we recommend a 2-stage cache: prefix KV for heavy reuse and secondary LRU slot for session context. that reduces repeated attention compute.
[07:45] Maya Rodriguez: sounds complex but promising. will the snapshot show cache hit rates?
[07:49] Priya Mehta: yes, hit/miss and effective token savings will be in the snapshot report.
[07:55] Sara Ng: what about multi-region routing — we have EU and NA users.
[07:59] Alex Chen: we support region-aware routing; you can pin EU traffic to EU clusters to meet residency. automatic fallback to nearest region if primary is saturated.
[08:10] Devon Price: residency requirements — we'll share which routes need EU-only residency.
[08:14] Maya Rodriguez: okay.
[08:16] Alex Chen: any blockers we haven't covered?
[08:19] Liam O'Connor: just the usual: network setup time, and getting the sanitized traces. otherwise good.
[08:26] Priya Mehta: one more note on quantization — aggressive quantization saves cost but we validate on your eval set to ensure quality isn't degraded for critical flows.
[08:36] Maya Rodriguez: we'd like to see a quality regression report if any changes are proposed.
[08:40] Priya Mehta: yep, we'll include quality benchmarks for any quant profile proposed.
[08:46] Alex Chen: wrapping up, let's recap action items and dates.
[08:50] Jordan Blake: recap: Priya perf snapshot due 11/20; Alex pricing by 11/17; Maya to share traces by 11/18; Devon to confirm SOC2/KMS by 11/19; Jordan to schedule pilot kickoff 11/24.
[09:08] Maya Rodriguez: confirmed. thanks team.
[09:11] Alex Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the security packet.
[09:16] (crosstalk)
[09:20] Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: automated speaker labels sometimes merged and occasional homophone errors (SOC two instead of SOC2, KV cash). we preserved hesitations and filler for authenticity.
